objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with abnormal behavior, difficulty swallowing, and involuntary movements.

turns.content: Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—let’s start: when did the abnormal involuntary movements and the difficulty swallowing begin, and have they been getting worse? Patient: Now please continue your dialogue Doctor: Do the movements include jerking or twisting of the face/arms/legs (chorea/dystonia), and are you having any fever, confusion, or recent infection or new medication (especially antipsychotics/anti-nausea drugs/levodopa)?

Patient: The involuntary movements and the difficulty swallowing began about a month ago, and they’ve been gradually getting worse. They look like twisting and jerking of my arms and face. I haven’t had fever or a recent infection, and I haven’t started any new medications recently.

Doctor: Thank you—are you having trouble speaking or drooling, and do you ever have episodes of sudden stiffness or spasms (especially in the jaw/neck) that feel triggered by stress or touch? Doctor: Also, have you noticed any weight change, new visual changes, or behavioral/personality changes over the same month?

Yes, I’m having trouble speaking and I’ve noticed more drooling, and I also get sudden stiffness and spasms in my jaw and neck that seem to be triggered by stress. Over the same month I’ve felt more confused, my personality has changed, and I’ve had weight loss. I haven’t had any new vision problems.

Doctor: Given the gradual worsening over a month with choreiform/twisting movements, dysphagia/drooling, stress-triggered jaw/neck spasms (likely dystonia/opisthotonus), plus confusion/behavior change and weight loss, I’m concerned about a neurologic disorder such as autoimmune/paraneoplastic encephalitis or prion disease rather than medication side effects—do you have a history of cancer (especially lung/breast/ovarian) or recent severe headaches/family members with similar illness? Doctor: REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain_with_contrast Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Lumbar_Puncture_CSF_with_cell_count_protein_oligoclonal_bands_and_paraneoplastic/autoimmune_encephalitis_panel (±14-3-3/RT-QuIC if available)

RESULTS: - Vital Signs: Temp 36.8°C (98.2°F); BP 130/85 mmHg; HR 72 bpm; RR 14 breaths/min. - Neurologic Examination: Mental status confused (oriented to person and place only); cranial nerves normal; motor system shows irregular, nonrepetitive, arrhythmic movements of neck and head; reflexes show delayed return to neutral ankle position after plantar reflex. - Brain MRI: Atrophy of the caudate nuclei with ex vacuo dilatation of the frontal horns of the lateral ventricles. - Genetic Testing: Positive for the huntingtin (HTT) gene mutation. - Requested tests (MRI with contrast; lumbar puncture/CSF encephalitis panel ±14-3-3/RT-QuIC): NOT PRESENT IN PROVIDED DATA (no results available).

Doctor: Your MRI finding of caudate atrophy with progressive chorea/dystonia, dysphagia/drooling, psychiatric/personality change, and confirmed HTT gene mutation indicates Huntington disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Huntington disease (HTT mutation–positive, caudate atrophy with progressive chorea/dystonia and neuropsychiatric symptoms)
